lines.text: A 4-tonne coin sank to the bottom of the sea, and people kept spending it. Would you accept it?
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: This is Yap, in the Pacific. Its money: rai, huge carved stone discs.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA
SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA
SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA
lines.speaker: bill

lines.text: So how do you pay with a coin you can't lift?
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: You don't move it. Everyone just agrees who owns it now.
chunks: Everyone just *agrees* who owns it now.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: They were cut on Palau, 400 km away, and carried home by sea.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: And one stone never made it home.
chunks: And one stone never made it home.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: It sank on the way. The islanders agreed it still existed, and kept trading it.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: That's the mirage: money was never the stone. It was the story everyone believed.
lines.chapter: SHORT: THE MONEY AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SEA

lines.text: Today, your money is mostly numbers in a computer.
chunks: Today, *your* money is mostly *numbers* in a computer.
